forecaster_note: Clean fun to decent sized peaky surf in the morning. More power PM but with light onshores. Short period south swell for some peaky head high or so surf at the south magnets this morning — smaller elsewhere, clean with offshore winds. Then expect some more power as long period S swell fills in through the afternoon as the shorter period stuff eases. Similar size: head high to a bit above by later afternoon as well, but a bit of bump with light onshore winds. — Hugh McDowell, Surfline

wind.summary: W offshore 9kph with 12kph gusts holding through the morning, going light variable S around midday (3kph) then ESE onshore 12kph from about 2–3pm. Clean window closes at lunchtime.

shark.summary: SharkSmart NSW layers read successfully this refresh (DPI Fisheries + SLSNSW drone), but the most recent detection anywhere in NSW is still dated 25 July — the feed has not published a new detection in 20 days, so no all-clear can be given. The last Northern Beaches entry was a shark observed at Long Reef Beach on 25 July (water evacuated). Tap through to check live before you paddle out.

days.label: Today
days.note: Best of it is happening right now. Energy peaked before dawn at 276 kJ and is bleeding away all day — 196 kJ at 9am, 177 by midday, 133 by 3pm — with the W offshore holding until roughly 11am before it goes light S and then ESE onshore around 2pm. Tide is draining off the 9:17am high, which is the good part of the cycle. Angle is 182° dead south again: Long Reef and Curl Curl get the size, Dee Why and Manly get the leftovers. If you can get wet before 11am, do it.

dee-why.window: Now until 11am. Offshore W, tide draining off the 9:17am high, 196 kJ still in the water. After midday the energy is under 180 kJ and the wind swings.

tip.label: Frontside at the Point — but manage expectations
tip.text: 196 kJ sounds respectable until you see where it comes from: 4.8ft @ 9s at 182°. Dead south is the angle that wraps into Dee Why fat and walls up instead of bowling. The little 0.6ft @ 17s at 180° is the one worth waiting for — long period wraps far better than the 9s slop sitting on top of it. Sit off the Point, let the short-period south mush go through, and pick the longer-spaced sets for your frontside rights. If you want size today you drive 5 minutes north.

alerts: 182° dead south — size does not translate here
Energy easing all day: 276 kJ pre-dawn to 133 kJ by 3pm
ESE onshore from ~2pm

long-reef.window: Now to 12pm. Pick of the four — the forecaster's 'south magnet' call is exactly this bank. Waist to head with the W offshore still on it.

tip.label: Go here — the south magnet
tip.text: Same 196 kJ Dee Why turns into waist-to-chest, Long Reef turns into waist-to-head. That is 182° swinging straight in rather than having to bend around the headland. 9s spacing is workable rather than good, so paddle for the sets and don't chase the in-betweens. Sets ease steadily after midday, and the ESE gets on it by 2pm — this is a morning call, not an all-day one.

alerts: Biggest of the four on this angle
Easing through the day — 133 kJ by 3pm
ESE onshore from ~2pm

curl-curl.window: Now to 12pm, then it drops to poor-fair by mid-afternoon. Look at the north end first.

tip.label: The bank lottery
tip.text: Curl Curl takes this south angle nearly as well as Long Reef and it is quieter mid-morning on a weekday. On a 9s south with the tide draining off a 1.4m high, the north end usually has the better shape — the south corner tends to close out on this spacing. Worth a drive-by look before you commit; if the sand is wrong, Long Reef is two minutes away.

alerts: Bank-dependent on a short-period south
Drops to poor-fair by 3pm

manly.window: Skip it. Thigh to waist all morning and poor-fair from midday.

tip.label: Backside on the lefts — not today
tip.text: North Steyne is the most shadowed of the four from 182°, and the numbers say it plainly: 1–2ft while Long Reef is running waist-to-head on identical energy. Nothing wrong with the wind or the tide here, there is just no swell reaching it. Save the backhand session for a proper NE–ENE pulse.

alerts: Smallest of the four — shadowed from the south
Poor-fair from midday

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: Reverse of today — a builder, not a fader. Only 76 kJ at dawn and 93 kJ at 9am, then it ramps hard: 191 kJ by midday and 237 kJ by 3pm as a new short and long period S pulse fills in. Hugh McDowell notes there is more long-period S in it than the spot forecasts show. The catch is wind: light SW offshore only until about 7am, cross-shore S from 9am and building to 16kph gusting 25 by mid-afternoon. Your 10am–12pm slot sits on the ramp with the wind still workable. Sheltered corners are the play once the S gets on it.

dee-why.window: 10am–12:30pm on the build, off the 9:57am high. Before 9am there is only 93 kJ in the water — it is genuinely small.
alerts: Building all day, not peaking until after the wind turns
S cross-shore from ~9am, 16kph gusting 25 by 3pm
Drops to poor-fair from midday as the wind gets on it

long-reef.window: 10am–1pm. Holds a fair rating the longest of the four as the S wind builds — the best weekend-morning option.
alerts: S wind builds through the afternoon
Poor-fair by 3pm despite 237 kJ

curl-curl.window: 10am–1pm if the north end bank is holding. The southern corner offers a bit of shelter once the S fills in.
alerts: S cross-shore from mid-morning

manly.window: The sheltered-corner play. Smallest through the morning but the only one still rated fair at 3pm — the Queenscliff end tucks under the S wind.
alerts: Smallest of the four in the morning
Best wind protection of the four in the afternoon

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Saturday is the weekend. It builds from 76 kJ at dawn to 237 kJ by mid-afternoon with the S wind arriving mid-morning, so 10am–1pm is your slot before the cross-shore ruins it. Sunday is bigger on paper — chest to overhead at Long Reef and Curl Curl — but the wind is E/ESE onshore from first light, 11kph at 9am and 19kph gusting 25 by midday, and every spot rates poor-fair all day. Take Saturday morning and write Sunday off unless you are just going for a paddle.

dee-why.window: Sat 10am–12:30pm. Sunday is onshore from dawn — chest to head but junk.
alerts: Sun: ESE onshore from first light, 19kph gusting 25 by midday
Sat: S cross-shore builds from ~9am

long-reef.window: Sat 10am–1pm is the weekend session. Sunday has the biggest surf of the three days and the worst wind of the three days.
alerts: Sun: biggest but onshore all day
Sat: fair until early afternoon

curl-curl.window: Sat late morning if the bank is right. Sunday onshore from dawn.
alerts: Closeout risk on the bigger Sunday sets
Sun: ESE onshore all day

manly.window: Sat is the pick here — the only spot still rated fair at 3pm Saturday. Sunday the ESE is straight onto it.
